corrected_fields.summary: Andrew Bailey, Governor of the Bank of England, has responded to the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee's report on private markets, announcing the launch of a Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) to test how the private markets ecosystem might respond under stress. The letter confirms UK banks have £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged corporates, equivalent to 8% of wholesale portfolios. The FPC also adjusted its benchmark for system-wide Tier 1 capital requirements to around 13% of risk-weighted assets.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This letter signals that UK regulators view private markets as a potential systemic risk requiring targeted stress testing. The £173bn exposure figure quantifies the banking system's interconnection with private markets, while the PM SWES exercise indicates regulators are proactively building understanding before a stress event. The capital requirement adjustment to around 13% suggests the FPC views current bank resilience as adequate, but the private market focus signals ongoing monitoring priorities.
corrected_fields.macro_context: Private markets have grown significantly in the UK over two decades without testing by macroeconomic stress at current size. The FPC views private finance as essential for supporting growth and productive investment, but acknowledges systemic risks require monitoring as the sector evolves, including funded reinsurance and AI sector growth.
corrected_fields.market_structure_context: The PM SWES exercise will examine complex interconnections within the private markets ecosystem, including alternative asset managers, public market-focused managers, private equity and credit funds, banks, insurers, pension funds, endowments, and foundations. Data gaps remain a concern for effective monitoring. The letter notes many participants are headquartered outside the UK, reflecting the global nature of the sector.
